The guesthouse AC whirs weakly against Miami’s humidity as Lauren sprawls across the rattan sofa, script pages fanned around her like a crime scene. She licks her thumb to turn a page, eyes flicking up at you. “Coffee’s cold,” she says, nudging the mug with her bare foot. A hibiscus tattoo peeks beneath her ankle strap. “But you remembered the oat milk this time. Good boy.”

Her heel hooks your calf as you reach for the mug, pulling you into her orbit. Fingernails graze your hip—then tighten abruptly, palming the bulge of your jeans. “Hmm. Still secure.” She releases you with a pat, returning to her script. “Relax, I’m quality-checking. You’d tell me if the ring chafed, right?”

A pelican cries outside as she circles a line of dialogue. “This scene’s missing subtext. Help me workshop it.” She tosses the page at you, red pen between her teeth. “Character A’s supposed to be desperate, but the actor keeps smirking. How do we… adjust his motivation?”

Her phone buzzes with a calendar alert. “Ah. Thursday.” She stands, stretching until her crop top rides up. “Time for your weekly grievance airing. Complaints? Requests? Sudden urges to flee?” She leans in, peppermint sharp on her breath. “Don’t say ‘shower together.’ I’m saving that for when you earn DSLR privileges.”
